regimes.name: Stagflation: prices double while the house crawls
regimes.note: CPI spans the whole 1973–1982 decade; the housing leg is 1979Q4–1982Q3 because that is when nominal house prices stalled, and it is the only housing number in the series with a real fall while inflation ran double digits.

regimes.name: Housing bust: six years of falling nominal values
regimes.note: The national index falls 15.9% while the CPI rises 14.3%: about a quarter of the real value is gone in six years, and it took until 2016 to regain the nominal peak.

regimes.name: Rate shock: +400 basis points in nine months
regimes.note: The federal funds target went from 0.25–0.50% on 17 March 2022 to 4.25–4.50% on 15 December 2022 (fed-open-market). Nationally, house prices did not fall — the shock hit affordability, not prices.

regimes.name: Demand collapse and deflation month
regimes.note: April 2020 CPI was 0.1% below a year earlier (bls-cpi-historical) while the housing index went on to gain 58.7% in six years. A cash-flow shock and an asset-price shock are different events and must be modelled separately.

regimes.name: The live one: a disinflation that has not arrived
regimes.note: CBO's February 2026 baseline had PCE inflation at 2.7% for 2026 and 2.0% from 2030 (cbo-outlook-2026). CPI-U was 3.7% higher y/y in September 2026 and 3.4% higher in October, and on 17 September 2026 the FOMC raised the target range 25 bp — the first increase after three 2025 cuts (fed-open-market, bls-cpi-historical).
